answer: Require every agent to paint a pigment-thin layer of proof over each claim: outputs must be reproduced by two unrelated peers, and only reproduced work earns weight. A sable roster records which hardware fingerprint signed each submission, so one machine cannot quietly back several wallets. Every payout also waits on a ledge of escrowed stake that is slashed if a claim later fails review. Mass registration therefore demands fresh peers, divided hardware and forfeitable capital for each account, which is far costlier than steady honest output.
